name: Learn: Runtime Security with Falco
description: Learn runtime threat detection with Falco step by step — deploy the Falco DaemonSet, find and read its rule files, author a custom rule that catches a shell in a container, trigger and detect the alert, then tune a rule with a macro/exception so known-good activity stays quiet.
objective: CKS › Runtime Security (20%). Goal: deploy Falco as a DaemonSet, locate its rule files, write a custom rule that detects a shell spawned in a container, trigger and observe the detection, and tune a rule with an exception — the behavioral-detection tasks the CKS weights heavily.

questions.title: Deploy Falco as a DaemonSet
questions.teach:
**Falco** watches syscalls and alerts when activity matches a rule. Because it must see *every* node's syscalls, it runs as a **DaemonSet** — one agent per node (a Deployment would miss nodes). The easy install is Helm: add the `falcosecurity` repo, then `helm install falco falcosecurity/falco -n falco --create-namespace --set driver.kind=modern-ebpf`.

**Gotcha:** `--create-namespace` only works with `helm install`; if the `falco` namespace already exists, drop that flag.
questions.prompt:
Install Falco as a DaemonSet in a namespace called `falco`, using the modern-ebpf driver.

Target: a DaemonSet exists in namespace `falco` whose pods run the Falco image (`kubectl -n falco get ds` shows it).
questions.hint: `helm repo add falcosecurity https://falcosecurity.github.io/charts && helm repo update`, then `helm install falco falcosecurity/falco -n falco --create-namespace --set driver.kind=modern-ebpf`. Check `kubectl -n falco get ds`.
questions.solution:
helm repo add falcosecurity https://falcosecurity.github.io/charts
helm repo update
helm install falco falcosecurity/falco --namespace falco --create-namespace \
  --set driver.kind=modern-ebpf
kubectl -n falco rollout status ds/falco
kubectl -n falco get ds,pods

verification.description: a Falco DaemonSet exists in namespace 'falco'

questions.title: Confirm Falco is running
questions.teach:
Confirm the DaemonSet actually scheduled a pod on every node. `kubectl -n falco get ds falco` shows `DESIRED/CURRENT/READY` **per node** (not replica counts) — `DESIRED` should equal your node count. `kubectl -n falco get pods -o wide` lists the per-node pods.

**Gotcha:** readiness is per-node — on a non-BTF host the modern-eBPF driver can't load, so pods schedule but never reach Ready. Here, scheduling is what's graded.
questions.prompt:
Confirm the Falco DaemonSet rolled out — one Falco pod scheduled on every node.

Target: the `falco` DaemonSet's `desiredNumberScheduled` > 0 (a pod per node). On a BTF-enabled host the pods also become Ready; on this bench the eBPF driver can't load, so scheduling is what's graded.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n falco get ds falco` — check `DESIRED`/`CURRENT` (one per node). `kubectl -n falco get pods` shows the per-node pods (they only reach Ready on a BTF host).
questions.solution:
kubectl -n falco get ds falco      # DESIRED = node count, one Falco pod per node
kubectl -n falco get pods -o wide # one falco-* pod scheduled on each node

verification.description: Falco DaemonSet rolled out (one pod scheduled per node)

questions.title: Write a custom rule: shell in a container
questions.teach:
A Falco `- rule:` needs `rule:` (name), `desc:`, `condition:`, `output:`, and `priority:`. The `condition:` is a boolean filter over syscall fields, and Falco ships reusable macros: `spawned_process` (an exec), `container` (inside a container), `shell_procs` (bash/sh/zsh/…). So a shell-in-container rule is `condition: spawned_process and container and shell_procs`. Add it to **`falco_rules.local.yaml`** (the `falco` ConfigMap) — never the shipped `falco_rules.yaml`.

**Gotcha:** name it exactly `Terminal shell in container` so the grader finds it.
questions.prompt:
Add a custom rule named `Terminal shell in container` to `falco_rules.local.yaml`. Its condition must detect a shell process spawned inside a container (use `spawned_process`, `container`, and `shell_procs`).

Target: the `falco` ConfigMap's `falco_rules.local.yaml` contains a rule named `Terminal shell in container` whose condition references `spawned_process`, `container`, and `shell_procs`.
questions.hint:
Edit the ConfigMap key `falco_rules.local.yaml` to add:
```
- rule: Terminal shell in container
  desc: A shell was spawned in a container
  condition: spawned_process and container and shell_procs
  output: "shell in container (user=%user.name container=%container.id)"
  priority: WARNING
```
then `kubectl -n falco rollout restart ds/falco`.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n falco get configmap falco -o yaml > /tmp/falco-cm.yaml
# append the rule under the falco_rules.local.yaml key, then apply. Example rule body:
cat <<'EOF'
- rule: Terminal shell in container
  desc: A shell was spawned in a container
  condition: spawned_process and container and shell_procs
  output: "shell in container (user=%user.name container=%container.id cmd=%proc.cmdline)"
  priority: WARNING
EOF
# after editing the ConfigMap:
kubectl -n falco rollout restart ds/falco

verification.description: rule 'Terminal shell in container' present with correct condition

questions.title: Trigger the rule and detect the alert
questions.teach:
Prove the rule fires: `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- sh` spawns a shell in a container, then `kubectl -n falco logs ds/falco | grep "shell in container"` shows the alert (Falco's default output is stdout). A rule is **enabled by default**; an explicit `enabled: false` (or commenting it out) silently stops detection even on a healthy DaemonSet.

**Gotcha:** observing the alert needs a running modern-eBPF probe, which needs a BTF kernel. This bench has no BTF, so the step is graded on the closest artifact — that the rule is **enabled** in the local rules.
questions.prompt:
Confirm the detection path is live: ensure the `Terminal shell in container` rule is enabled in `falco_rules.local.yaml` (not `enabled: false` and not commented out), so that execing a shell into a pod would produce an alert in Falco's logs.

Target: in the `falco` ConfigMap, the `Terminal shell in container` rule is present and enabled (RUNTIME detection requires a BTF host — graded here on the enabled rule artifact).
questions.hint: If you added `enabled: false` or commented the rule out, re-enable it. A Falco `- rule:` entry is enabled by default; an explicit `enabled: false` under it disables it. Then `kubectl -n falco rollout restart ds/falco` and, on a BTF host, `kubectl exec -it <pod> -- sh` then `kubectl -n falco logs ds/falco | grep 'shell in container'`.
questions.solution:
# Trigger (works on a BTF host):
kubectl run trip --image=busybox:1.36 --restart=Never -- sleep 3600
kubectl exec -it trip -- sh -c 'echo hi'
# Detect (BTF host):
kubectl -n falco logs ds/falco | grep "shell in container"
# Here (no BTF): make sure the rule is enabled in falco_rules.local.yaml
kubectl -n falco get configmap falco -o jsonpath='{.data.falco_rules\.local\.yaml}'

verification.description: rule 'Terminal shell in container' is enabled (closest artifact; live detect needs BTF host)

questions.title: Tune the rule with an exception
questions.teach:
Known-good shell activity (a health-check script) causes false positives. **Tune** the rule instead of deleting it. The native way is an `exceptions:` list on the rule: each entry has a `name:`, `fields:` (syscall fields to check), optional `comps:` (operators), and `values:`. A match in any exception makes the rule **not** fire. Alternatively, `and not <macro>` the condition.

**Gotcha:** `fields`, `comps`, and `values` must line up, and `in`-style values are bracket-wrapped, e.g. `values: - [my-healthcheck]`.
questions.prompt:
Tune `Terminal shell in container` so a process named `my-healthcheck` does not fire the rule. Add an `exceptions:` entry named `known_good` on the rule (listing `proc.name`), or add a macro and `and not ...` it into the condition.

Target: the `falco` ConfigMap's `falco_rules.local.yaml` contains either an exception named `known_good` or a tuning macro, referencing `my-healthcheck`.
questions.hint:
Under the rule add:
```
  exceptions:
  - name: known_good
    fields: [proc.name]
    comps: [in]
    values:
    - [my-healthcheck]
```
or define `- macro: allowed_shell_procs` with `condition: proc.name in (my-healthcheck)` and append `and not allowed_shell_procs` to the rule condition. Then `kubectl -n falco rollout restart ds/falco`.
questions.solution:
# Append exceptions to the rule in falco_rules.local.yaml:
cat <<'EOF'
- rule: Terminal shell in container
  desc: A shell was spawned in a container
  condition: spawned_process and container and shell_procs
  output: "shell in container (user=%user.name container=%container.id)"
  priority: WARNING
  exceptions:
  - name: known_good
    fields: [proc.name]
    comps: [in]
    values:
    - [my-healthcheck]
EOF
kubectl -n falco rollout restart ds/falco

verification.description: exception/macro for 'my-healthcheck' present in local rules
